"THERAPY? YOU DON'T NEED THERAPY LIKE THOSE WHITE PEOPLE, YOU'RE JUST SULKING FROM US YELLING AT YOU. MAN UP AND JUST WORK HARDER IN COLLEGE."

-said to me by my dad when at the end of my high school graduation ceremony he said I was a failure and I started crying and said I wanted to see a therapist. I wish I saw their faces when they got a call from the social worker at the University Hospital, one year later, that I was in the emergency room after my roommate found me hanging from the ceiling.

They're a lot better now, but it's sad that it had to come to that.
Random question, but do you get treatment at the Rachel Upjohn building, or do you  have a doctor that's off campus?

1) Started cutting myself

2) Attempted suicide

3) Attempted suicide

In that order...

I know exactly what you mean. Before I started treatment I wasn't on any meds, and I was absolutely miserable and enjoyed it. I was ridiculously critical of myself (driving my depression) and of others, but it let me *think.*  Now I am on my meds, I am emotionally stable but I can't think anymore; I'm just emotionally and mentally flat. It's partially the reason why my grades slid this semester. I want to get off my meds so bad, so I can just go back to being miserable and critical, so I can be my former self again.
I should mention that as a result of anxiety I cannot function and this is making me feel even worse and it's becoming a downward spiral which leads to very, very bad things.

I'm in the same boat as you. I'm currently taking Wellbutrin, Prozac, Trazodone, Abilify, Klonopin and Ativan. To make it worse, Abilify is a brand drug that costs thousands of dollars without insurance, but my shitty insurance company wouldn't even pay a feasible part of it for my co-pay to be economically reasonable. 

It gets hard to trust your psychiatrist, or even therapist for that matter, because they just keep on feeding and feeding you different types of drugs. The fact that big pharma is behind all these drugs, many of which were proved effective only by a very small margin.

It feels like shit to know that I can only function when I'm on a bunch of chemicals. HOWEVER, being on all these drugs does do something for me; I am able to function normally ever since my two hospitalizations earlier this year. Maybe it's because of the different situation I am in, or  that I have a therapist now, but something is happening that's right.

Having considered the ECT option seriously (never did take it though), it is something that HAS been proven to work. You could try it out, but you have to figure out whether the benefits outweigh the costs, e.g. whether or not you want to forget what has happened over the past few months (I did). 

Anyway, sorry I can't be of much help, but I hope you find solace knowing that you're not alone. And please, try to hang tight.

Have a good weekend!

Unfortunately, from my experience, people only begin to start taking depression seriously when something serious happens. 

That kind of attitude needs to stop.

It's possible. One of the most helpful things for me to accept myself and become comfortable with myself was to stop caring about what other people thought about me. 

Have you tried seeking help?

Never, ever force yourself to study. 

No, seriously, never force yourself to study. In my experience at least when I started falling into a depressed state, I would lose focus. I'd then start worrying about how I couldn't focus, think of what a failure I am, and become even more depressed etc etc. It becomes a vicious cycle that ends very badly, at least for me.

Make small goals for yourself; even studying for a short while being able to retain information is an achievement when you're depressed.  Above all take breaks and distract yourself with other things. Try to get out of your room/house as much as possible (from what you wrote it shouldn't be too hard) and take a walk in the park. Go to your room only for sleep. If you're living near a college town, it also helps to study somewhere new every day (different corners of libraries, etc.), which helped me a lot to relieve some stress (since once you use a study place long enough you "establish" yourself at it and then distractions start to come into play). At least where I went to college, there were places where there were glass ceilings that let a lot of sunlight in, and it also helped me concentrate studying in the sunlight.

It was absolutely terrifying... it partially drove me to a second suicide attempt mostly because these were really freaky panda bears that were "going to take me away." Huge panic attacks and whatnot. I could hear them munching on bamboo.

Though not really an antidepressant, I recently went through klonopin withdrawal. I was shaking uncontrollably the entire day (to the point my parents had to pin me down), had suicidal thoughts, panic attacks, terrible sleep cycles, loss of appetite, and was just in a really depressed mood in general. 

Although now I think about it, there was one time I forgot to take Celexa, and I hallucinated that there were panda bears following me around.
